spec.description: How many people use betula.app. Loki's ruler counts them from Traefik's access log (config/monitoring/loki-rules) and stores the numbers in Prometheus; this dashboard only reads those. Provisioned from deploy/config/monitoring/grafana/dashboards - edit there.

spec.title: Device, last 7 days
spec.description: Phone (iPhone, Android with Mobile), Tablet (iPad, Android without Mobile), Desktop. iPads that ask for the desktop site count as Desktop.

spec.title: Requests: Google, crawlers, rest
spec.description: All requests to betula.app per hour. "Crawlers turned away" got 403 from the crawler filter in front of the site: only search engines and link previews are served (deploy/config/traefik/dynamic/crawlers.yml), and nothing from the clouds whose crawlers pass for browsers (crawler-networks.yml). "Outside Europe" got 403 for where it came from (europe.yml). Neither counts as a visitor. "Other crawlers" are those other search engines and link previews. "Everything else" is people plus scanners and tools without a crawler user agent.

spec.title: Crawlers by name
spec.description: Requests in the range by crawler, served or turned away: the word with bot/crawl/spider in its user agent. Google's renderer sends a Nexus 5X agent without that word.

spec.title: Visitors, last 24 h
spec.description: Browsers (address + user agent) that started the app in the 24 hours before the end of the range.

spec.title: Visitors, last 7 days
spec.description: Browsers that started the app in the 7 days before the end of the range. Counted once an hour.

spec.title: App starts
spec.description: Every start of the app in the range, returning visits too.

spec.title: Active calendar subscriptions
spec.description: Feed addresses a calendar fetched at least twice in 7 days and also in the last 48 hours. Counted once an hour.

spec.title: Visitors, rolling 24 h
spec.description: At each point: browsers that started the app in the 24 hours before it.

spec.title: Visitors per hour
spec.description: Browsers that started the app in each hour.

spec.title: The pass: the catalog's download
spec.description: Requests for the catalog (/api/db) and for the pass (/api/pass) per hour, by what they got (folia/crates/server/src/pass.rs, since Folia 1.107.0). "Catalog refused without a pass": 401 and a challenge, no byte of the catalog. "Pass earned": a solved challenge, 204 and the cookie. "Solution refused": a challenge too old, of another network or not solved. "Catalog downloaded": 200, with a pass. "Catalog unchanged": 304, the browser has it. A browser on its first visit makes one refused, one earned and one downloaded; whatever is refused far more often than passes are earned is no browser running the app.

spec.title: The pass: addresses
spec.description: Addresses (as Traefik saw them) per hour that were refused the catalog without a pass, that earned a pass and that downloaded the catalog. Addresses refused that never earn a pass ran no script: those are what the pass keeps away.

spec.title: The traps: what Folia turned away
spec.description: Requests Folia itself answered 429 per hour, and pauses ended by the page's button (folia/crates/server/src/trap.rs, since Folia 1.109.0). "Trap sprung: laid bait": somebody asked for the link nobody sees or for the address the data worker's script names and never asks for (/api/trap/). "Trap sprung: scanner probe": .env, .git, WordPress, PHP and the like, the list of the dashboard "Security". "Turned away while paused": any other request from an address a trap paused, for an hour. "Pause ended by the button": somebody at a paused address pressed "Weiter zu Betula". Traefik's own rate limit is not counted.

spec.title: The traps: addresses turned away
spec.description: Addresses (as Traefik saw them; IPv6 addresses of one /64 count one by one here) Folia answered 429 in each hour: those that sprang a trap and those that asked while paused.
